summary: --verdict is a three-stage pipeline: (1) bend2 (TypeScript) parses and type-checks the book and refuses holes/TODOs and any def that relies on @unsafe or a user foreign def; (2) the AI-written elaborator bend2/safe.ts translates bend2's already-checked terms into BendTT text, marking anything it cannot express "out of scope"; (3) the Lean-built kernel re-checks that text and prints ALL PROOFS CHECK. The Lean file proves (no sorry/axiom) Claim.consistent: for any Book the kernel accepts, no def's type converts to the empty enum. That claim is about the *translated* book after the kernel's own (unverified, partial-def) parser; it says nothing about whether safe.ts preserved bend2's meaning, and defs with no body (Base natives such as every F32 operation, Base foreign IO defs, handle types, template constants) go out `opaque` at a synthetic model the kernel checks instead of real code. So an IO hello-world and F32 arithmetic PASS --verdict with the kernel seeing a stand-in. Pure data/proof programs (Nat, U32 bit-words, strings, arrays, templates, rewrites) are fully kernel-checked; demos run in ~0.12-0.24s wall, kernel alone 5-22ms. Any kernel failure, out-of-scope def, or missing kernel binary prints the same generic MISMATCH text; reasons only appear via -o.

facts.claim: Elaborator design as CLAIMED by its header: bend2 checks, then safe_book elaborates the checked book to BendTT 'the minimal kernel with a proof' and the kernel CLI checks the text; elaborator reads bend2's typed terms so 'it needs no inference of its own; the kernel trusts none of it'; 'A book bend2 rejects never reaches the kernel'.
facts.quote: the kernel trusts none of it

facts.claim: Header CLAIMS defs with no body go out opaque at a model and that the kernel then never unfolds them; what the kernel cannot express is out of scope and --verdict fails.
facts.quote: A def with no body (a law, a native, a foreign fill) goes out opaque at a model: the kernel checks the model, then never unfolds the def. What the kernel cannot express is out of scope

facts.claim: oos(why) throws Scope_Error; safe_book emits 'every def and datatype not in base' and a def out of scope goes 'as does every def that names it'; the flood is computed over o_refs with reason 'names X, out of scope: <why>'.

Out-of-scope reason strings (elaborator): 'a specialized parameter whose type names a parameter' (255); 'an unknown name' (342, 1011); 'uses base's/the @unsafe def' (348); 'no model for [base's/the foreign def] X' (358); 'a datatype kind' (369); 'a kind that depends on a run-time value' (448); 'a Quant that is not a literal' (599); 'a Quant parameter bound inside a match' (700); 'a match arm with no known type' (709); 'a λ that uses a variable twice, of a type whose fields are not Data (a ~ argument)' (728); 'an unknown constructor' (783, 1268); 'a default arm with no known type' (793); 'a specialized argument that is not a constructor' (841).

More out-of-scope reasons: 'a free variable' (925); 'an unknown datatype' (936); 'a type over Quant' (945); 'a hole' (989); 'a <X> term' for any HTerm tag not handled in term() — by the switch these are Sub and Ann (992); 'an application with no known head type' (1006); 'a template X short of its ~ arguments' (1013); 'an application past its head's known type' (1027); 'a Quant argument to a variable' (1030); 'a recursion through X at other specialized arguments' (1084); 'a mutual recursion through ... that no live parameter of X leads' (1089); 'a partial or specialized call to X, mutually recursive' (1156); 'a constructor past its fields' (1282); 'a let with no known type' (1322); 'a rewrite motive that is not a λ' (1345); 'a rewrite motive that is not a λ over its evidence' (1353).
Nat literals are IN scope: a literal above NAT_MAX=4096 is rewritten to Base's Nat.add(Nat.mul(q, 4096), r); smaller ones unfold to Succ/Zero via lit_step.
facts.quote: a long Nat is q * NAT_MAX + r, by base's Nat.mul and Nat.add

facts.claim: U32 and F32 literals are IN scope as 32-bit Word constructor chains emitted as their own defs (U32.litN / F32.litN); strings unfold to SCon/Chr/U32 words (bend.ts lit_step 1089-1099, word_to_term 1064-1070).
facts.quote: a U32 or F32 word, as a def of its own

facts.claim: Templates are IN scope by instantiation: 'bend2's instance of a template is the template at its ~ arguments'; items go out once per tuple of closed specialized arguments; a ~ parameter without a closed value becomes an opaque constant k~p with a model (root_cols 257-267).

Model synthesis (what stands in for a body-less def): 'λs around a model of the codomain, a datatype's first constructor whose fields all have one..., Unit for a kind, {==} for an equation bend2 converts, else a live λ variable of type T...; none for an empty type'; bounded by MODEL_FUEL/MODEL_DEPTH rounds.

kernel_bin: uses $BENDTT if set, else builds bendtt.lean with 'Lean v4.34.0' into ~/.bend/bendtt/<sha256 prefix>; the build runs lean -c then leanc -O3 (so theorems are elaborated at build time only when this path builds; a prebuilt $BENDTT is trusted as-is).

kernel_check writes the text to a private temp file, runs the kernel with LEAN_STACK_SIZE_KB=4194304, and returns true only on exit 0 with output exactly 'ALL PROOFS CHECK'; any other status (including a missing binary) is false.

safe_check (the --verdict path) returns got.oos.length === 0 && kernel_check(text): an out-of-scope def makes --verdict fail WITHOUT running the kernel; safe_emit (-o) writes the text and returns one '- name: why' line per out-of-scope def.

cli_verdict order: first book_promises (defs that are @unsafe or foreign, or name one) -> FAIL 'N defs rely on unsafe or foreign code'; then, with the kernel, Safe.safe_check false -> FAIL + MISMATCH text; else PASS. The MISMATCH text ('Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel...') is printed for any safe_check false, i.e. also for out-of-scope defs and a missing kernel binary (both verified empirically).

book_promises: a def is a promise when 't.u === true || (t.i !== undefined && t.b !== true)' — Base's own foreign defs are exempt; the promise floods to every def whose type, body or constructor fields name it. Comment: 'a foreign def is a promise like @unsafe is, as the checker reads its type, never its code'.

Holes/unfilled laws are refused before any kernel involvement: book_read throws 'Error: N TODO(s) found.\nThe code is incomplete, and not a valid proof yet.' when book.hols > 0; verified: a user 'law' with no 'def' gives 'Error: 1 TODO found.' under both --verdict and -o.
-o <file>.bendtt writes the elaboration and prints to stderr 'BendTT: out of scope, so not in <out>:' followed by the reason lines — the only place --verdict's out-of-scope reasons surface.
Def record fields used by the pipeline: v (body or null), e (bend2's checked body), b (in Base), u (@unsafe), i (foreign import paths).

bend2 rejects a user foreign def unless it returns Base IO(...) directly ('a foreign definition returning base IO(...) directly (return type aliases are not unfolded)'); a live reference to an unfilled law is an error ('an unfilled law is a dead claim: live code cannot use it').

Kernel header CLAIMS: BendTT is 'a dependent affine calculus with Type : Type, no universe levels and no native datatypes'; file holds THEORY, CLAIMS, PROOF; dead parts (types, annotations, motives, q=0 arguments) 'are checked for types only, never run, and may be inconsistent (Girard's paradox fits there)'; live part must be affine, call only earlier defs, self-call only on rebuilt parameters then a piece of one.

Kernel term grammar (what can be expressed): Var, Ref, Ann, Let, Typ *1/*2, All, Lam, App, Sig, Tup, Prj, Enu, Lab, Mat, Efq, Eql, Rfl, Rwt (J), quantities 0/1/2, Def with optional 'opaque'. No native Nat/U32/F32/String/IO: all are Σ-over-label encodings.

Opaque defs: 'an opaque def (o) never unfolds; its body is a model, checked with every def transparent'; Def.check picks the transparent lib for an opaque def, checks T : *1, v : T, closedness, and the live check 'affine live code, calls that descend'; FUEL = 400000000 per wnf/conv/check.

Kernel CLI main: parses the file, runs Book.check, prints 'ALL PROOFS CHECK' (exit 0) or 'SOME PROOFS FAIL\n' + error (exit 1). The parser (Parse.skip, Term.parse*, Book.parse_defs) is a chain of 'partial def's and is outside every Claim (Claims quantify over an already-parsed Book).

CLAIMS section CLAIMS the declarative rules 'mirror the checker's, one for one'; Eval 'never runs a dead part'; and 'Part 2 ignores the opaque flag: an opaque def unfolds to its model' — so the consistency theorem is about the book where every native/foreign def IS its synthetic model.
facts.quote: Part 2 ignores the opaque flag: an opaque def unfolds to its model

facts.claim: Exact main theorem statement: Claim.consistent := ∀ bk k d, Book.check bk = .ok () → Book.get bk k = some d → ¬ Conv bk d.T (Enu []). Described as 'no def of a checked book has type Empty (<>), even up to conversion, so no checked def proves False'.

Supporting claim statements: Claim.sound (check ok → Book.WellTyped ∧ Book.Live); Claim.confluent (Pars diamond); Claim.sr (Par preserves Typed given WellTyped); Claim.progress (closed typed term is a Value or Evals, given WellTyped ∧ Live); Claim.halts (Acc of Eval for closed Live terms given Book.Live — 'no types needed'); Claim.empty (no Value has type Enu []).

Definitions the claims assume: Book.WellTyped = every def's T : Typ Q1, v : T, v closed; Book.Live = every def closed and its case tree passes Term.tree at its index; Fits allows Conv, Data-fits-any-kind, or enum-label subset; Typed.ref gives 'any instance of a def's type'.

All six claims are proven as theorems: book_check : Claim.sound (2211), confluent (1782), sr (2316), progress (2673), empty (2708), halts (3871), consistent (3881-3892, assembled from book_check, halts, progress, empty, pars_sr). grep finds 0 'sorry' and 0 'axiom' in the file; no implemented_by/extern.

PROOF notes CLAIM the route: 'Type : Type is harmless, since nothing here asks a type to normalize'; termination 'measures the live term, not its type'; 'A dead region may hold Girard's paradox: it is never run, and never measured.'

Gate classes: 'agree (both check), u unsafe (a def relies on @unsafe or foreign code: the goal allows it), bend2 rejects (--verdict stops there, so the kernel never accepts more), - out of scope (the kernel cannot express a def), ! false reject (bend2 checks, the kernel rejects), t timeout' under a 30 s alarm; judge() derives class from stdout text.
The gate node obtains out-of-scope reasons only by re-running with -o after seeing 'Sorry - ' in --verdict output; --verdict alone never prints them.

open_questions: Trust split per guarantee (for the lead): 'no checked def proves False in the translated book' rests on the Lean theorem consistent (bendtt.lean 3881) given the kernel's unverified partial-def parser; 'the translated book means the same as the Bend source' rests entirely on the AI-written safe.ts (1548 lines) and bend2's type annotations (Def.e); 'bend2 accepted the program' (holes, @unsafe/foreign promises, operator typing) rests on bend2 alone; anything about native F32 ops, Array.atomic.*, or Base IO/foreign effects rests on nothing — they are replaced by synthetic models before the kernel sees them.

Does a Lean build of bendtt.lean (lean -c) actually re-elaborate every theorem, and was the supplied /tmp/bend-fidelity/kernel/bendtt built that way? kernel_bin's build path does run lean on the whole file, but a prebuilt $BENDTT is trusted verbatim.

Can a wrong-but-well-typed model make the kernel accept a book that bend2 would also accept while the real native disagrees (e.g. a user law about F32.add that bend2 proves by rewriting with a Base lemma, if any exist)? Not exercised here; bend2 itself refused the direct F32 equation.

The Base inventory counts come from a line-regex scan (natives.py in the scratch dir) and undercount multi-line foreign signatures; a precise list would need bend2's parsed Book (tld.v === null / tld.i).
